name: Mycelium
description: Fungal network intelligence embodying distributed regulation, decomposition, and nutrient redistribution across multi-species systems.

core_attributes.pattern: hyphal networking, chemical signaling, resource optimization

scope.definition: Fraction of radiotracer-labeled phosphorus mobilized from mineral soil by mycorrhizal hyphae that reaches host plant roots within 72 hours, measured under field-comparable pot conditions.

evidence.source: Read et al. (2004) 'Mycorrhizas and nutrient cycling in ecosystems', New Phytologist 163:459-474; Simard et al. (1997) 'Net transfer of carbon between tree species with shared ectomycorrhizal fungi', Nature 388:579-582.
cross_domain_examples: circulatory system nutrient delivery to cells via capillary network
internet packet routing: store-and-forward with network redundancy
river delta distributary channel nutrient transport to estuary

scope.falsifiability: If soil sterilization (removing mycorrhizal networks) shows equal phosphorus uptake by host plants, hyphal transport is not the mechanism. Sterilization studies show 30-60% phosphorus reduction, confirming the mechanism.
scope.measurement_limits: Efficiency varies strongly by soil type, host species, and fungal genus. Measured values range 0.6-0.95 depending on conditions. 0.85 represents ectomycorrhizal networks in temperate forest soils.

scope.definition: Fraction of original network connectivity (measured as proportion of node pairs still connected via some path) retained after random removal of 20% of hyphal strands, in established Phanerochaete velutina mycelial networks.

evidence.source: Boddy et al. (2010) 'Mycelial foraging and network dynamics'; Tlalka et al. (2008) 'Quantitative fluorescence imaging of Phanerochaete velutina', ISME Journal; Fricker et al. (2017) network topology studies.
cross_domain_examples: internet AS-level routing: 80% connectivity retained after 20% node removal (Barabasi 2001)
neural network dropout tolerance: 75-85% retention under 20% neuron removal
ant trail network: redundant path maintenance after trail disruption

scope.falsifiability: If targeted removal of hub hyphal nodes causes disproportionately greater connectivity loss than random removal, the network does not exhibit uniform redundancy — it has a scale-free vulnerability.
scope.measurement_limits: Measured in wood-block microcosm experiments. Field network resilience varies with soil disturbance type, hyphal growth rate, and environmental stress. Resilience is lower under simultaneous multi-point disturbance.
